fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled Mach-O file is read from offset 0 into the Mach_header structure mhdri.
Magic value must match MH_MAGIC (0xfeedface for 32-bit) plus address-size offset; attacker controls this field.
cputype must match the expected architecture (e.g., CPU_TYPE_I386=7 for 32-bit x86).
filetype must match the expected Mach-O file type (e.g., MH_EXECUTE=2).
Attacker-controlled ncmds value is extracted from the Mach header; must be >= 2 to reach the vulnerable second iteration.
Attacker-controlled sizeofcmds becomes the remaining-bytes counter headway; must pass validation (>=16, <= file_size, <= MAX_N_CMDS).

fine_trace.code: if (!ncmds || MAX_N_CMDS < ncmds || file_size < headway || headway < 4*4) throwCantUnpack(...);
fine_trace.note: Validation passes with ncmds>=2 and headway>=16; attacker chooses headway such that after first command, remaining bytes < 8.
Heap buffer of exactly sizeofcmds bytes is allocated and filled with attacker-controlled load-command data.
Pointer to the start of the heap-allocated load-command buffer.

fine_trace.code: for (unsigned j=0; j < ncmds; ptr = (Mach_command const *)(ptr->cmdsize + (char const *)ptr), ++j) {
fine_trace.note: Loop iterates ncmds times; pointer advances by cmdsize each iteration. Attacker sets first command's cmdsize so that headway becomes 4 (e.g., sizeofcmds=16, first cmdsize=12).
First 4-byte read of the second load command; with headway=4 this read is within bounds but consumes the last 4 bytes.
Second 4-byte read at offset ptr+4; with only 4 bytes remaining in the heap buffer, this reads 4 bytes past the allocated rawmseg_buf, causing the heap-buffer-overflow.
The 4-byte out-of-bounds read is performed by get_ne32 (or get_le32 for little-endian) when accessing ptr->cmdsize past the heap buffer boundary.

fine_trace.code: if (is_bad_linker_command(cmd, cmdsize, headway, lc_seg, sizeof(Addr))) { ... throwCantUnpack("file corrupted"); }
fine_trace.note: The OOB read has already occurred before this validation; is_bad_linker_command may throw, but the heap-buffer-overflow is already triggered by the read of ptr->cmdsize.
